quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake on the good tire.
Speed up to get off the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the good tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a conflict with other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic. Be extra alert where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of the following, except:

options.text: Meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fit snugly all the way around, and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you just like other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about being seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and hard to see. For your safety, ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust?

options.text: Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is usually located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider will slow down or stop. This hand signal can be used instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to keep the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to keep the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit makes it easier to brake quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you if you fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide what to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Turning too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is usually to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The most important thing to help others see you at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to accelerate but more time to stop.
It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
It takes more time to accelerate but less time to stop.
It takes less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out between cars.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation under normal riding conditions. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Ensures the other driver will properly yield to you.
Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means another driver will properly yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear boots or sturdy shoes tall enough to cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels that won't catch on foot pegs or road surfaces. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take very little time.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will continue to run like new if it is properly maintained. Make routine inspections part of your regular maintenance schedule.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs about road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.
